The corpse trial of Pope Formosus (The Cadaver Synod): In 897 AD, Pope Stephen VI had the rotting corpse of his predecessor exhumed, dressed in papal robes, and placed on trial for treason, culminating in a horrific public desecration.

The Mad Gasser of Mattoon: During WWII in Illinois, an entire town was gripped by mass hysteria and terror over an elusive phantom attacker who allegedly sprayed a paralyzing, sweet-smelling gas into people's bedroom windows.

The 1902 eruption of Mount Pelée and the survival of Ludger Sylbaris: A devastating volcanic eruption wiped out an entire Caribbean city of 30,000 people in minutes, leaving only a convicted murderer saved by the thick walls of his poorly ventilated dungeon cell.

The execution of György Dózsa: In 1514, after leading a failed peasant rebellion in Hungary, the charismatic leader was condemned by the nobility to sit on a red-hot iron throne and crowned with a burning iron crown, while his starving followers were forced to eat his flesh.

The deadly panic of the 1897 Bazar de la Charité fire: A devastating blaze sparked by a cinematograph projectionist's mistake trapped Paris's high-society elite inside a wooden bazaar, leading to a brutal, every-man-for-himself struggle for survival in the heart of the Belle Époque.

The Tarrare Gluttony Crisis: In 18th-century France, a military medical experiment on a former street performer with an insatiable, monstrous appetite goes horrific when he is suspected of swallowing a 14-month-old hospital patient alive.
